title: Adaptive request-momentum trace gate and sampled-span throttle for SDKs
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Introduce an SDK-level adaptive gate that limits trace emission for high-throughput ephemeral requests ("momentum gate") and a complementary sampled-span throttle to bound downstream telemetry volume without losing critical causality information. This ticket covers design, SDK implementation (Node/Python/Go), integration tests, and a phased rollout via canary and release channels in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Momentum gate activates under configurable QPS/failed-request thresholds and reduces sampled spans emitted by >= 65% for noisy endpoints while preserving at least one root span per request group.
SDK implementations provide a single consistent API for instrumentation libraries to opt into the gate, with minimal changes to existing integrations.
End-to-end tests validate propagation of trace-context (trace-id, parent-id, sampling decision) across HTTP/gRPC and WebSocket paths when the gate is active.
Console dashboard surfaces gate activation rates, span drop counts, and per-route sample retention metrics within the latency/error dashboards.
Rollout plan completed with a canary cohort (5 teams) and a fallback mechanism to disable the gate remotely.
Documentation and release notes published in Confluence + changelog.
Performance: SDK overhead < 0.25ms median per-instrumented request when gate inactive, and <0.5ms when active (measured on our standard microservice benchmark).
design_notes: Momentum gate is based on a moving-window QPS estimator combined with a recent-error-rate heuristic to prioritize noisy/erring endpoints for sampling reduction.
We keep deterministic selection for root spans: each request group (by hash of service+route+minute) guarantees one retained root span to preserve causal visibility.
Throttle uses a token-bucket algorithm per SDK instance with soft-fallback: if downstream telemetry pipeline reports backpressure, SDK reduces local emission further.
Propagation: do not mutate trace-id; use a new header 'x-rwin-sample' to annotate SDK-local sampling adjustments while honoring W3C traceparent for interoperability.
Security: no payload data is changed; header usage reviewed with security for PII risk (link in 'links').
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement momentum gate prototype in SDK core (Node + Python). Expose config knobs: qps_window_seconds, qps_threshold, error_rate_threshold, min_retained_per_bucket.
Phase 2 (week 3): add sampled-span throttle (token-bucket) and integrate with existing batching/async exporter logic.
Phase 3 (week 4): extend to Go SDK and add guardrails for serverless cold-start scenarios.
Phase 4 (week 5): add telemetry signals (gate_as_active, spans_dropped, retained_roots) to the internal metrics pipeline and wire to Console dashboards.
Phase 5 (week 6): QA, integration tests across HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket, and rollout to canary teams.
Implementation notes: keep gate decision deterministic and idempotent to avoid flip-flopping on retries; prefer dropping child spans over roots when thresholding.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable gate for 5 internal services under feature flag for 72h; monitor retained root ratio and error-impact signals.
Soft rollout: expand to 25% of SDK instances across latency-critical customers if no regression.
Full rollout: staged by customer tier with remote-config default off for P0 customers until validated by SRE.
Fallback: remote-config boolean to turn gate off immediately; emergency runbook with contact list and dashboard links.
Communication: notes to customers via Console banner + changelog on GA.
KPIs to monitor: span ingestion volume, pipeline backpressure alarms, 99th-percentile tail latency, error-rate delta for gated endpoints.
testing_plan: Unit tests for moving-window QPS estimator and token-bucket throttle (coverage >= 90%).
Integration tests: end-to-end trace propagation through HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket while gate active; verify at least one root retained per group.
Load tests: verify span-drop rate and SDK CPU/memory under synthetic traffic patterns (bursty and steady).
Chaos tests: simulate downstream exporter failure and confirm SDK reduces emission and recovers correctly.
Benchmarks: microbench harness to measure per-request overhead in both active/inactive gate modes.
Manual QA: runbook steps for canary validation documented in Confluence link.
